profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility, referred to in public mapping data as Lumen Santa Clara, is located at 3045 Raymond Street, Santa Clara, CA 95054, per public property records; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites, treating those specifications as commercially site-dependent rather than public data. This entry is a separate Santa Clara-area building from the Duane Avenue Lumen site also tracked in this registry, both part of Silicon Valley's dense colocation and carrier-hotel submarket.

California regulators are actively reworking how large data center loads are billed and interconnected as demand grows statewide. Under SB 57 (2025), the California Public Utilities Commission opened a rate-design rulemaking in April 2026 addressing electric rate impacts of data centers and other large transmission-connected loads; the California Independent System Operator separately published a formal issue paper on large-load interconnection considerations in January 2026.

reading.body:
Lumen Santa Clara is a carrier-neutral colocation facility in the dense Silicon Valley market, located at 3045 Raymond Street in Santa Clara. Lumen does not publish power capacity or square footage for this site or any of its 175-plus North American colocation facilities, treating those specifications as commercially site-dependent rather than public data. The facility operates in the 3 to 15 kilowatt per cabinet range typical of Lumen's network-centric edge colocation product, which differs structurally from the wholesale hyperscale campuses tracked for AI infrastructure planning.

California regulators are actively reworking data center interconnection and rate design as demand grows statewide. The California Public Utilities Commission opened a rate-design rulemaking in April 2026 addressing electric rate impacts of data centers, and the California Independent System Operator published a formal issue paper on large-load interconnection considerations in January 2026. These regulatory developments apply to the entire state grid constraint, not to Lumen Santa Clara specifically, but affect the cost and feasibility of scaling any facility in the region.

Without published capacity figures for this site, it cannot be ranked among California's disclosed data center infrastructure. California has 103 mapped data center facilities, 11 with published megawatt figures totaling 365 MW. Lumen Santa Clara's absence from the published capacity record means its contribution to state AI infrastructure planning is opaque, and the site should be treated as a known location in the carrier-hotel market rather than as a quantified resource for AI scaling analysis.
